messages:
trevor: Noticing weird tail latency spikes on preemptible lanes in eu-west this morning. Looks correlated with a handful of tenants getting repeatedly requeued after short-lived evictions.

anne: Ugh. Are these thermal/drain evictions or cloud preemptions?

trevor: Cloud preempts mostly. But the pattern is odd — same tenants get requeued onto hot nodes repeatedly, so their KV-cache regen + long warmups are amplifying neighbor impact.

lucas: Do we have a metric that captures 'requeue churn' per tenant?

maria: Not exactly. We have alloc_requeues but it's per-node. We should surface per-tenant requeue_rate and a short-window warm_cache_miss_rate.

trevor: Agreed. Proposal: detect "preemptible_drift" = tenants with >3 requeues in 10m AND tail latency p95>2x baseline. Flag them and route new requests to fractional dedicated slices for 30m.

anne: Fractional dedicated sounds expensive. Cost/benefit?

trevor: It will cost a few hours of warmpool hours for the slice, but prevents noisy spread and KV thrash across the rack. Cheaper than repeated retries + customer impact.

lucas: Implementation: small controller that watches eviction events + requeue counts. When condition met: set tenant.routing_hint = "shielded_slice" and throttle its soft-affinity to hot racks. Rollback after 30m of stable metrics.

maria: We should be careful with tenant SLAs. Add a safety throttle: if tenant is on Dedicated paid plan, skip auto-shield and alert SREs instead.

anne: Also need a telemetry patch to tag impacted KV cache misses in traces so we can validate. Minimal rollback path ok?

trevor: I'll sketch the controller PR. Pseudocode:
```
watch(eviction_events)
compute tenant_requeues[tenant] over 10m
if tenant_requeues[t] > 3 && p95_tail[t] > baseline*2:
  annotate tenant as preemptible_drift
  set routing_hint(t) = \"shielded_slice\"
  emit alert to #eng-oncall with summary
```

lucas: Nice. Add a cooldown to avoid flip-flop: 45m cooldown after a shield.

ops-bot: Deploy pipeline triggered for branch trevor/preemptible-drift-controller. CI: running.

maria: For rollout: canary in eu-west-1 only, 1% of tenants, with an opt-out tag so solutions engineers can exempt sensitive workloads.

anne: I'll update runbook: how to manually remove shield, check requeue count, and escalate to infra leads if we see >5 shields in 6h.

lucas: Also add a cheap cost-metering log so finance can estimate incremental warmpool spend. Tag as opt-in until we have numbers.

trevor: Cool. I'll open the PR and link runbook edits. If CI passes, let's canary tonight at 03:00 UTC.

maria: FYI: I'll subscribe alerts into the new SLO channel so product teams see degradation hints.

trevor: Thanks — will post a short follow-up with PR link and canary checklist. :thumbsup:
